newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura gives PPABank buy rating.
newsitem.headline: Nomura gives PPABank buy rating.

text.p: Investors should buy shares of Polish bank First Polish-American Bank SA PPABAnk, which should lift net profits to 13.5 million zlotys this year from 9.1 million in 1996, Nomura Equity Research said in a report.
"Prospects for 1997 are good, with expected profit growth of 48 percent," the report dated January 14 said, adding that PPABank should earn 17.1 million zlotys next year.
Nomura said a good sign was the bank's 1996 loan growth of 88 percent, as well as its net earnings growth of 160 percent.
It said the bank's share price, depressed in last year's final quarter due to severe Polish interest rate volatility and the firm's one-for-four rights issue, should soon rebound.

"We expect a strong share price recovery following the completion of this issue," the report said about the issue which began on Monday and ends on February 3 or March 10, depending on whether or not the first leg is fully subscribed.
Nomura said PPABank shares, which closed on the main market on Wednesday at 17.2 zlotys, would rise to their relevant trading range of between 20 and 25 zlotys.

It said the bank also benefited from its unique focus on Poland's small business segment, giving it better growth opportunities than any other Polish bank and from funding and capital commitment support from its 53 percent owner, the Polish American Enterprise Fund.
